Provenance:Property from the estate of Rafeeuddin Ahmed, New York, New York.Mr. Rafeeuddin Ahmed had a long and distinguished diplomatic career, serving with the Pakistan Foreign Service from 1955-1969, and in 1970 embarked on the first of several distinguished roles within the United Nations Secretariat, spanning over 30 years. Between 1955 and 1968, he served at the Embassies of Cairo, Ottawa, and Beijing. Mr. Ahmed was highly respected by colleagues and those who came to know him. He was a valued mentor and a great believer in the power of multilateralism and international cooperation, and, as a tribute from the World Tourism Organization (UN Tourism) notes, “…leaving behind a legacy defined not only by institutional achievement, but by humanity, wisdom and grace.”来源：纽约市外交家拉菲乌丁·艾哈迈德（Rafeeuddin Ahmed，1932—2026）遗产。巴基斯坦资深外交家艾哈迈德供职于联合国体系逾三十年，以副秘书长级别工作二十一年，是国际多边外交领域的重要人物之一。艾氏毕业于巴基斯坦旁遮普大学，后赴美国塔夫茨大学深造，专攻国际经济与国际法。1954年他以政治学讲师身份开启职业生涯，次年加入巴基斯坦外交部，1955至1969年间先后派驻开罗、渥太华及北京等地。1970年进入联合国秘书处，历任开发计划署高级顾问、经济及社会理事会秘书、秘书长办公厅主任、亚太经济社会委员会执行秘书等职。艾氏多次受命处理复杂国际事务，参与过东帝汶、柬埔寨、老挝—泰国冲突及缅甸等地区的调停。在1982年福克兰群岛危机和伊朗人质事件中发挥了重要作用。2003年又被任命为伊拉克问题特别顾问。他在2026年逝世，一生成就卓著，评价极高。本场委托的中国艺术品购自1960年代派驻北京巴基斯坦使馆任内。

Provenance:Property from the estate of Rafeeuddin Ahmed, New York, New York.Mr. Rafeeuddin Ahmed had a long and distinguished diplomatic career, serving with the Pakistan Foreign Service from 1955-1969, and in 1970 embarked on the first of several distinguished roles within the United Nations Secretariat, spanning over 30 years. Between 1955 and 1968, he served at the Embassies of Cairo, Ottawa, and Beijing. Mr. Ahmed was highly respected by colleagues and those who came to know him. He was a valued mentor and a great believer in the power of multilateralism and international cooperation, and, as a tribute from the World Tourism Organization (UN Tourism) notes, “…leaving behind a legacy defined not only by institutional achievement, but by humanity, wisdom and grace.”来源：纽约市外交家拉菲乌丁·艾哈迈德（Rafeeuddin Ahmed，1932—2026）遗产。巴基斯坦资深外交家艾哈迈德供职于联合国体系逾三十年，以副秘书长级别工作二十一年，是国际多边外交领域的重要人物之一。艾氏毕业于巴基斯坦旁遮普大学，后赴美国塔夫茨大学深造，专攻国际经济与国际法。1954年他以政治学讲师身份开启职业生涯，次年加入巴基斯坦外交部，1955至1969年间先后派驻开罗、渥太华及北京等地。1970年进入联合国秘书处，历任开发计划署高级顾问、经济及社会理事会秘书、秘书长办公厅主任、亚太经济社会委员会执行秘书等职。艾氏多次受命处理复杂国际事务，参与过东帝汶、柬埔寨、老挝—泰国冲突及缅甸等地区的调停。在1982年福克兰群岛危机和伊朗人质事件中发挥了重要作用。2003年又被任命为伊拉克问题特别顾问。他在2026年逝世，一生成就卓著，评价极高。本场委托的中国艺术品购自1960年代派驻北京巴基斯坦使馆任内。

Butterman (E&J Frankel's attorney), New York, New York, acquired from E&J Frankel, January 14, 2004.This lot was acquired by the present owner, Mr. Jay Butterman, from the well-known dealers of Chinese works of art Edith and Joel Frankel. Mr. Butterman, who was their friend and family attorney, fondly recalls the Saturday gatherings at their Madison Avenue gallery, where customers and friends would come together to chat and admire Frankel’s latest acquisitions. Among the regulars at these Saturday gatherings were important scholars and artists such as the great artist and collector C.C. Wang and the renowned calligrapher and scholar Wang Fangyu, both of whom exhibited their work at the Frankel gallery. He has particularly fond memories of fascinating discussions with the psychologist and television personality Dr. Ruth Westheimer, who was a dear friend of the Frankel’s and wrote an essay for the catalogue for their Exhibition called “Play It Again, Asian Games and Pastimes” which received much attention including a significant review in the New York Times. A collector of antiquarian books and Asian art since his youth, Mr. Butterman is a distinguished attorney and has, in his long career, represented numerous important artists, galleries, and collectors in a variety of capacities.  We are privileged to present these important pieces in addition to early Chinese ceramics, other scholarly items, and Japanese works of art from Mr. Butterman’s collection.來源：紐約州紐約市Jay R. Butterman先生（傅蘭閣古董行家族律師）藏， 2004年1月14日購自紐約傅兰閣。巴特曼先生是著名的婚姻法和家庭法律師，多次入選“紐約超級律師”名列，著名古董商傅蘭閣夫婦生前一直由他代理，關係相當親密。據他説傅蘭閣夫婦鼎盛時期，每周六在家辦餐會招待親朋好友兼畫家學者，王方宇、王几千都是常客，一起围观傅蘭閣新到的文房精品。本場徵集到巴特曼先生所藏中國瓷雜，敬請關注。

Provenance:-The first: Golden Moment Auction, Ontario, CA, June 26, 2019, lot 209 -The second acquired from a Hong Kong dealer, 1973-Both: Property from the Estate of Dr. Thomas Klein, sold to benefit Jefferson Hospital湯姆·克萊因醫生收藏鼻烟壺逾四十年。他畢業於哈佛大學與羅徹斯特大學，曾於美國陸軍擔任婦產科醫師並出任高階領導職務。其後於傑佛遜醫院服務三十年，2023年以婦產科副主任身分榮退，期間培養了五百餘名住院醫師與無數醫學生。他的學術與臨床精神延續於以其名設立的「Thomas A. Klein 講席教授」，本場拍賣所得亦歸於傑佛遜醫院。Tom Klein’s life was shaped by two enduring passions: medicine and the collecting of snuff bottles. While these worlds rarely intersected, both were marked by the same qualities—quiet dedication, discernment, and grace. Tom was unfailingly modest–when the I.C.S.B.S. held its convention in Philadelphia, he entrusted me to select bottles from his collection for the exhibition “Embers of the East,” a task made challenging by the number of exceptional bottles. His passion for collecting was thoughtful rather than acquisitive, grounded in appreciation rather than display. These were his companions—objects he handled, studied, and loved for over 40 years.Professionally, Tom enjoyed an equally distinguished career. A graduate of Harvard University and the University of Rochester, he served as an obstetrician-gynecologist in the U.S. Army in senior leadership roles. He spent thirty years at Jefferson Hospital, retiring in 2023 as Vice Chair of Obstetrics and Gynecology, having trained more than five hundred residents and countless medical students. His legacy continues through the Thomas A. Klein, MD Professorship in Quality and Safety in Women’s Health. To those who knew him as a collector, these accomplishments mirrored the man I admired: principled, generous, and exacting without pretension. Over the 35 years I had the privilege to know him, he was a gentleman in the most absolute sense of the word. Though he is deeply missed, his presence endures in the objects he cherished and in our shared love of snuff bottles.Clare Chu

-The first, Republic Period, porcelain of upright rectangular form, with a cylindrical neck, gilded mouth and protruding faceted rectangular footrim, the main sides each with a gilt-framed rectangular panel in famille-rose enamels, depicting on one side a scholar standing under a willow tree observing his attendant making tea on a brazier, the reverse with a poetic inscription followed by two seals (Qianlong) in iron-red enamel, the remainder of the bottle decorated with enamels imitating puddingstone, the base with an apocryphal blue enamel Qianlong nian zhi mark
-The second, 19th century, porcelain modeled as a crouching squirrel with grapes, the body finely carved and enameled in gray with darker markings, the eyes picked out in black
-The third, mid-late 19th century. Porcelain of tapering rounded-rectangular form, the shoulders sloping to a cylindrical neck, with a flat lip and protruding oval footrim, each main side finely painted in iron-red with differing images of Zhong Kui, one as the Demon Queller brandishing a sword, the reverse in his official robes, a bat flying above; the base with a four-character Qianlong mark in iron-red
-The fourth, circa 1780-1850. Porcelain, molded, carved and reticulated, of ovoid form with a flared neck, a flat gilt lip and a protruding oval footrim, reticulated and carved on each main side in high relief with two ladies and eight children, well detailed and enameled in Famille Rose colors, on a terrace beneath palm leaves, a key-fret border encircling the neck, the base with a four-character Qianlong mark in iron-red script, attributed to the Imperial Palace kilns, Jingdezhen

Three Chinese Amber Snuff Bottles, 18th to 19th Century

清中期 琥珀鼻烟壺三支

Property from the Estate of Dr. Thomas Klein, sold to benefit Jefferson Hospital

description_block:
Four Chinese Snuff Bottles, Primarily 19th Century

清晚期 鼻烟壺四支

-The first circa 1820-1900, coconut shell of bulging tapering square section, skillfully assembled in panels, with a cylindrical neck, flat lip and protruding square footrim, the well-patinated body with applied mask-and-ring carvings to two opposing sides, the remainder undecorated.
-The second circa 1840-1880, sharkskin or shagreen of flattened ovoid shape, with a short neck, flat lip and flat base, the attractive covering evenly applied with joins on the narrow sides.
-The third, 19th century, possibly later. Horn of flattened ovoid form, with a slightly waisted neck, flat lip and base, the butterscotch body with dark brown and russet streaks, carved on the main sides in low relief to depict Buddhist symbols (ashtamangala) within an oval border, the narrow sides with bats
-The fourth, circa 1820-1900, coconut shell of slightly bulging tapering faceted form, with a short cylindrical neck, flat lip and protruding oval footrim, the body hexagonally faceted, undecorated except for well-carved and applied mask-and rings on two of the opposing facets.

Two Chinese Cinnabar Lacquer Snuff Bottles, 18th Century

清中期 剔紅鼻烟壺兩支

-The first: circa 1780-1860, cinnabar lacquer of spade form, with a flat lip, cylindrical neck and protruding oval footrim, the body finely and deeply carved to depict, on the main sides, a phoenix in flight amidst clouds, the narrow sides with elongated rocky promontories, the neck encircled with pendant acanthus leaves; probably Imperial

description_block:
Five Chinese Puddingstone Snuff Bottles, 18th to 20th Century

清中期-民國 抱子石鼻烟壺四支

-The first, circa 1750-1860, of miniature flattened-rounded form, the shoulders sloping to a cylindrical neck, with a flat lip, wide mouth and flat foot, the undecorated stone with numerous pebbles of various sizes and shapes, in shades of black, gray and brown, tightly embedded in a tan matrix, well-hollowed
-The second, 19th century, of shield form, with a waisted neck, flat lip and base, the narrow sides flattened, the undecorated body consisting of a rich russet-brown matrix embedded with dark brown pebbles of various sizes and shapes, many within a lighter shell.
The third, late 20th century, of tall, tapered cylindrical form with flared lip, flat mouth, indented circular foot, the stone of greyish pebbles in an ochre matrix
-The fourth, 19th–20th century, of ovoid form, the shoulders sloping to a slightly splayed neck, with a concave lip and flat base, the brown matrix embedded with small beige pebbles of various sizes and shapes, some with russet centers. 
-The fifth, possibly second half 19th century, of flattened rectangular form with rounded shoulders, cylindrical lip, flat mouth and protruding oval footrim, underside inscribed Xingyouheng Tang, which may be translated as "Hall of Perseverance or Constancy". The stone of a grainy beige matrix enclosing pebbles of various hues
Note:
According to the entry for a black lacquer snuff bottle, inscribed with a similar mark from the Francine and Bernald Wald collection, sold at Bonham's, New York, September 15, 2025, lot 157, the mark 'Xing You Heng Tang' refers to the hall of the fifth Prince Ding Zaichuan, poet, collector and patron of the arts, A great-great grandson of the Qianlong Emperor, Prince Ding rose to high official rank of his own accord during the Daoguang and Xianfeng reigns. 

Tallest height without stopper 3 1/4 in., 8.3 cm.

Property from the Estate of Dr. Thomas Klein, sold to benefit Jefferson Hospital

description_block:
Four Chinese Rock Crystal Snuff Bottles, 18th to 19th Century

清中期 水晶鼻烟壺四支

-The first, early 19th century, of elongated flattened rounded-rectangular form, the shoulders sloping to a cylindrical neck, with a concave lip and protruding oval footrim, the flawless transparent body undecorated on the main sides, the narrow sides with well-carved mask-and-rings, extremely-well hollowed
-The second, 19th century, of flat double-gourd shape, the shoulders sloping to a cylindrical neck, the lip flat, the clear stone very well hollowed, with the hollowing closely following the outline of the bottle.
-The third, circa 1750-1860, of flattened-rectangular form, the shoulders sloping to a cylindrical neck, flat lip, the recessed foot surrounded by an oval protruding footrim, the stone undecorated and almost flawless, very well hollowed.

description_block:
Four Chinese Glass Overlay Snuff Bottles, 18th-20th Century

清 套料鼻烟壺四支

-The first, late 19th century, glass of flattened rounded-rectangular form, the shoulders sloping to a waisted lipped neck, with a flat lip and protruding oval footrim, the body opaque white with single brown overlay carved with a sage and his attendant standing beside a tree and a two-character seal, the reverse with a scholar on horseback and his walking attendant crossing a bridge, the narrow sides with elongated mask and mock-ring handles, the lip and footrim also carved from the overlay. Possibly Yangzhou.
-The second, circa 1780-1850, glass of flattened ovoid form, the shoulders sloping to a cylindrical neck, the lip flat, the recessed foot surrounded by a neatly carved oval footrim, the caramel-brown body overlaid in emerald green, finely carved to depict a continuous scene of lotus leaves, pods and flowers rising from waves, the footrim also carved from the overlay.
-The third, 20th century, possibly later, glass of small ovoid form, with a wide mouth, flat lip, slightly everted neck and protruding oval footrim, the black body with a well-carved bright green and chartreuse overlay depicting continuous leafy vines with gourds, the footrim also carved from the overlay, the base with a four-character incised mark in seal script
-The fourth, 19th century, glass of circular form, the shoulders sloping to a slightly waisted neck, with a concave lip and protruding oval footrim, the bubble-suffused body with well-carved overlay of playful monkeys in six colors, the footrim also carved from the overlay

Largest height without stopper 2 7/16 in., 6.2 cm.

While these worlds rarely intersected, both were marked by the same qualities—quiet dedication, discernment, and grace. Tom was unfailingly modest–when the I.C.S.B.S. held its convention in Philadelphia, he entrusted me to select bottles from his collection for the exhibition “Embers of the East,” a task made challenging by the number of exceptional bottles. provenance: Property from the Estate of Dr. Thomas Klein, sold to benefit Jefferson Hospital. The first: Bonhams Los Angeles, September 2, 2020, lot 56. subject_matter: snuff bottles, ruby glass, amber glass, circular shape, pear shape, rounded-rectangular form, flat lip, oval footrim, faux handles, interior residue
description_block:
Four Chinese Ruby and Amber Glass Snuff Bottles

寶石紅及琥珀料鼻烟壺四支

-The first, circa 1770-1820, probably Imperial, attributed to the Beijing Palace Workshops, ruby glass of flattened circular (“moon-flask”) form, the shoulders sloping to a waisted neck, with a wide mouth, flat lip, and concave base surrounded by a protruding oval footrim, the ruby-red body undecorated, with interior soiling.
-The second, 18th century, possibly Yongzheng period, ruby-red glass of flattened pear shape, the shoulders sloping to a cylindrical neck, with a flat lip and protruding oval footrim, the body undecorated except for rudimentary rings on the narrow sides, the interior extensively crizzled, with snuff residue.
-The third, Early 19th century, amber glass snuff bottle of rounded-rectangular form, with rounded shoulders, cylindrical neck, concave lip and protruding oval footrim, the undecorated material in skilfull imitation of amber, with thin walls.
-The fourth circa 1730-1820, probably Imperial, attributed to the Beijing Palace Workshops, of ruby glass of circular (“moon-flask”) form, the shoulders sloping to a slightly waisted neck, with a flat lip and protruding oval footrim, the ruby-red body undecorated on the main sides, the narrow sides finely carved with faux handles, each depicted as a small loop suspending a ring. 

Largest Height without stopper 2 7/16 in., 6.2 cm.

Provenance:Property from the estate of Rafeeuddin Ahmed, New York, New York.Mr. Rafeeuddin Ahmed had a long and distinguished diplomatic career, serving with the Pakistan Foreign Service from 1955-1969, and in 1970 embarked on the first of several distinguished roles within the United Nations Secretariat, spanning over 30 years. Between 1955 and 1968, he served at the Embassies of Cairo, Ottawa, and Beijing. Mr. Ahmed was highly respected by colleagues and those who came to know him. He was a valued mentor and a great believer in the power of multilateralism and international cooperation, and, as a tribute from the World Tourism Organization (UN Tourism) notes, “…leaving behind a legacy defined not only by institutional achievement, but by humanity, wisdom and grace.”来源：纽约市外交家拉菲乌丁·艾哈迈德（Rafeeuddin Ahmed，1932—2026）遗产。巴基斯坦资深外交家艾哈迈德供职于联合国体系逾三十年，以副秘书长级别工作二十一年，是国际多边外交领域的重要人物之一。艾氏毕业于巴基斯坦旁遮普大学，后赴美国塔夫茨大学深造，专攻国际经济与国际法。1954年他以政治学讲师身份开启职业生涯，次年加入巴基斯坦外交部，1955至1969年间先后派驻开罗、渥太华及北京等地。1970年进入联合国秘书处，历任开发计划署高级顾问、经济及社会理事会秘书、秘书长办公厅主任、亚太经济社会委员会执行秘书等职。艾氏多次受命处理复杂国际事务，参与过东帝汶、柬埔寨、老挝—泰国冲突及缅甸等地区的调停。在1982年福克兰群岛危机和伊朗人质事件中发挥了重要作用。2003年又被任命为伊拉克问题特别顾问。他在2026年逝世，一生成就卓著，评价极高。本场委托的中国艺术品购自1960年代派驻北京巴基斯坦使馆任内。

description_block:
Ding Yanyong (Chinese, 1902-1978)

丁衍庸（近代，1902-1978）

Su San in a Cangue
Ink and color on paper, mounted on silk, Titled Su San Qi Jie, dedicated to Meilan Nvdi, signed and with one seal upper right

Note:
The present work depicts the high point of the famous Beijing Opera story of Su San, "Su San Leaving Hongtong County", where she is being led away as a prisoner and recounting her tragic tale of love and deceit. Under torture, she has been compelled to falsely admit to the poisoning of the wealthy merchant to whom she had been sold as concubine, framed by the merchant's jealous wife, all after she and her lover, the scholar Wang Jinglong, had been forced to part.

Image 32 3/4 x 11 3/4 in., 83.2 29.7 cm.

Provenance:Property from an important American Collection, gifted from the artist in 1975-1976.In 1975 and 1976, the collector, an American photographer, and her husband worked in Hong Kong on an artist’s grant and fellowship study, respectively. The American artist soon became one of Ding's first Western pupils. Ding gave her the Chinese sobriquet 'Meilan' or 'Beautiful Orchid', and this name appears as part of the dedication on many works. The collector and the artist became quite close, and Ding gave her mounted scrolls and more informal rapid studies. Freeman's/Hindman are delighted to offer works that have not been seen since the 1970s.來源：畫家於1975年贈與現藏家。1975-1976年，現藏家——一對美國攝影師伉儷，在香港學習藝術。經友人引薦結識丁衍庸，成為丁的首位西洋弟子。丁為之取名“美蘭”，師徒情深，贈畫頗多，且附上款。

description_block:
Zhang Yan (Qing Dynasty)

張儼（清）

Beauty in the Style of Qiu Ying
Ink and color on silk, framed and glazed.
Signed Zhang Yan, one artist's seal, dated 1800. Three colophons and multiple collectors' seals.
張儼
（清）
小青圖
絹本設色，鏡框
款識：乳燕調雛出畫檐，游蜂喧翅入珠帘。日長無事人慵困，寳鴨香消嬾更添。嘉慶五年（1800）嵗在庚申七月之朔。驀仇十州意于粳雪山房。張儼。
鈐印：澹庄
題跋：
（1）少年曾读小青诗，不信张郎会画眉。如此容颜如此态，当时却付画工儿。省斋吴大振和韵。
鈐印三
（2）低首摊书坐画楼，美人工笑亦工愁。谁传无限伤心事，妙笔能令终古留。春园新题。
鈐印三
（3）乙丑小春余于禾郡偶得此帧，虽时人摹寫，其用筆秀潤，猶可亞於實父也。張公本綉水諸生，每寄于毫端，豈悒怏之，深盍似小青乎，燈下漫係一絕。未詳觀史與觀詩何事卿卿，斂素眉不是佳人情脈脈。只緣弄筆著書兒。妙果山半農書題。
鈐印二

Provenance:Property from the estate of Rafeeuddin Ahmed, New York, New York.Mr. Rafeeuddin Ahmed had a long and distinguished diplomatic career, serving with the Pakistan Foreign Service from 1955-1969, and in 1970 embarked on the first of several distinguished roles within the United Nations Secretariat, spanning over 30 years. Between 1955 and 1968, he served at the Embassies of Cairo, Ottawa, and Beijing. Mr. Ahmed was highly respected by colleagues and those who came to know him. He was a valued mentor and a great believer in the power of multilateralism and international cooperation, and, as a tribute from the World Tourism Organization (UN Tourism) notes, “…leaving behind a legacy defined not only by institutional achievement, but by humanity, wisdom and grace.”来源：纽约市外交家拉菲乌丁·艾哈迈德（Rafeeuddin Ahmed，1932—2026）遗产。巴基斯坦资深外交家艾哈迈德供职于联合国体系逾三十年，以副秘书长级别工作二十一年，是国际多边外交领域的重要人物之一。艾氏毕业于巴基斯坦旁遮普大学，后赴美国塔夫茨大学深造，专攻国际经济与国际法。1954年他以政治学讲师身份开启职业生涯，次年加入巴基斯坦外交部，1955至1969年间先后派驻开罗、渥太华及北京等地。1970年进入联合国秘书处，历任开发计划署高级顾问、经济及社会理事会秘书、秘书长办公厅主任、亚太经济社会委员会执行秘书等职。艾氏多次受命处理复杂国际事务，参与过东帝汶、柬埔寨、老挝—泰国冲突及缅甸等地区的调停。在1982年福克兰群岛危机和伊朗人质事件中发挥了重要作用。2003年又被任命为伊拉克问题特别顾问。他在2026年逝世，一生成就卓著，评价极高。本场委托的中国艺术品购自1960年代派驻北京巴基斯坦使馆任内。

material: Watercolor on thin paper with thin fabric backing
provenance: Hill Auction Gallery, Sunrise, Florida, November 30, 2016, lot 246.
subject_matter: musician, street lamp, urban landscape, brick wall, stucco wall, light, texture, human figure, backdrop, performance
description_block:
Chen Chi (American/Chinese, 1912-2005)

程及（美籍華裔，1912-2005）

Musician under a Street Lamp, 1956
Watercolor on thin paper with thin fabric backing, signed in Chinese and English, with one seal, and dated lower left; in a Newcomb-Macklin Co., New York silvered carved wood frame, glazed.

Note:
The present work illustrates themes which the artist was particularly interested in exploring during the 1950s. The sense of space and light, presented in a theatrical way, perhaps referencing the shallow space of a stage, bounded by a curtain or backdrop, is physically enlivened by the texture of the urban landscape, focusing on the weathered surfaces of brick and stucco walls. In some of these works from the 1950s, like "Musician under a Street Lamp", the artist has included human figures, rendered in similar tones to their surroundings, grounding them in their environment. For other examples of this theatrical depiction of urban "stage sets", see Taipei, National Museum of History, Chen Chi, 1988, pp. 17, 18, 20-21, 26, 32, and 37. The last work cited, "Playing a Violin" is closely related to the present painting, with a seated violinist, dwarfed by the wall behind them, performing in the urban landscape.

Sheet: 32 1/2 x 30 in., 82.5 x 76.2 cm.; Frame 37 x 34 1/4 in., 94 x 87 cm.

This lot is located in Philadelphia.

provenance: Property from the Collection of Drs. Thomas and Patricia B Ebrey, Seattle, Washington.
subject_matter: rickshaws, people, signs, street scenes, trees, bicycles, shops, architecture, urban life, cultural heritage
description_block:
Three Works by David Bloch, comprising Shanghai (1945), Rickshaws (1945), and David Ludwig Block, Holzschnitte, Woodcuts, Shanghai 1940-1949.

1945-1949 大衛·布魯赫《上海》木刻兩種及參考書一種

David Ludwig Bloch (1910–2002) was a German-born American ceramicist and visual artist whose work reflects both exquisite technical mastery and a life shaped by displacement. Born in Floss, Germany, Bloch attended Munich’s renowned School of Applied Arts, where he trained in commercial and fine art before being dismissed under Nazi anti-Jewish policies. In November 1938, he was arrested during Kristallnacht and transported to Dachau concentration camp, where he remained until his release the following year. Shortly thereafter, he was expelled from Germany and emigrated to Shanghai, one of the few places that accepted Jewish refugees without a visa.

In Shanghai, Bloch re-established his artistic career, working as a designer for local printing and advertising firms while continuing to produce paintings and prints documenting the refugee experience. After the war, he immigrated to the United States in 1949, settling in New York and later Massachusetts. There, he became a respected ceramic artist, developing innovative forms and glazes and exhibiting widely across the country.

Bloch’s later work frequently returned to themes of memory and survival, including a series of stark, expressionistic prints depicting Kristallnacht. His art has been collected and exhibited by institutions such as the United States Holocaust Memorial Museum, the Leo Baeck Institute, and the Jewish Museum Berlin.

上世纪三、四十年代，为了逃避纳粹法西斯对犹太人的种族清洗，两万多德国、奥地利犹太人背井离乡来到上海避难，年轻的艺术家大卫·布鲁赫就是其中的一个。

布鲁赫1910年生于巴伐利亚Floss 小镇，自幼失去了父母，三岁时又因生病失去听力，童年时在慕尼黑皇家聋哑学校学习手语，后来考入了慕尼黑实用美术学院学习设计和版画。他曾和德国女孩玛莎相爱，生下女儿麗蒂娅，但纽伦堡法案严禁德国人和犹太人通婚，他们不得不分开。1938 年11 月9 日希特勒发动“水晶之夜”，布鲁赫和成千上万的犹太男人一起被关进达豪集中营。被释放后他只身乘船逃亡到日本占领的上海，在这个陌生的东方城市領略到中国人友善。

他没有着迷于十里洋场的歌舞升平，而是用画笔和木刻刀记录了老上海的民俗风情。在一次聋哑人的聚会上，布鲁赫遇到上海女孩郑小姐，他们用手语交流，1946 年成婚，几年后移民美国。布鲁赫2002 年下世，留有数百幅绘画和木刻版画，大部分是他在上海的九年当中制作的。關於他的作品與生平，參見加籍华人导演、中央美术学院电影与影像艺术系创建系主任王水泊2018年完成的紀錄片《大卫·布鲁赫》(David Bloch)。

artwork_title: An Impressive Japanese Household Shrine, Meiji Period, Dated 1880
provenance: Katsura Archéologie et Antiquités d'Asie, Paris, France, November 11, 2000. Property from the Collection of Donald G. McNeil Jr., Brooklyn, NY. Acquired from above and accompanied by two shipping documents.
subject_matter: Japanese shrine, Amitabha Buddha, bodhisattvas, flying cranes, stylized clouds, gold lacquer, wooden architecture, tripartite sanctuary, domed roof, decorative drawers
description_block:
An Impressive Japanese Household Shrine, Meiji Period, Dated 1880

The rectangular shrine surmounted by an openwork panel intricately carved with flying cranes amidst stylized clouds, set above double-hinged doors opening to reveal a secondary set of interior louvered doors. Crafted from hinoki (cypress) wood, the doors open to a tripartite sanctuary sheltering a central standing figure of Amitabha Buddha flanked by two seated bodhisattvas. The figures are set beneath a domed roof with exposed beams invoking traditional Buddhist temple architecture, supported by four columns against gold lacquered interior walls. The entire structure is raised on a stepped base fitted with six gold-lacquered drawers, the gilt lacquer wass added later in 1908.

Height 62 1/2 x width 30 5/8 x depth 20 3/4 in.

Property from the Collection of Donald G. McNeil Jr., Brooklyn, NY.

This lot is located in Philadelphia.

Butterman先生（傅蘭閣古董行家族律師）藏。1990年初購自蘇富比。巴特曼先生是著名的婚姻法和家庭法律師，多次入選“紐約超級律師”名列，著名古董商傅蘭閣夫婦生前一直由他代理，關係相當親密。據他説傅蘭閣夫婦鼎盛時期，每周六在家辦餐會招待親朋好友兼畫家學者，王方宇、王几千都是常客，一起围观傅蘭閣新到的文房精品。本場徵集到巴特曼先生所藏中國瓷雜與日本工藝精品，敬請關注。

Provenance:Property from the estate of Rafeeuddin Ahmed, New York, New York.Mr. Rafeeuddin Ahmed had a long and distinguished diplomatic career, serving with the Pakistan Foreign Service from 1955-1969, and in 1970 embarked on the first of several distinguished roles within the United Nations Secretariat, spanning over 30 years. Between 1955 and 1968, he served at the Embassies of Cairo, Ottawa, and Beijing. Mr. Ahmed was highly respected by colleagues and those who came to know him. He was a valued mentor and a great believer in the power of multilateralism and international cooperation, and, as a tribute from the World Tourism Organization (UN Tourism) notes, “…leaving behind a legacy defined not only by institutional achievement, but by humanity, wisdom and grace.”来源：纽约市外交家拉菲乌丁·艾哈迈德（Rafeeuddin Ahmed，1932—2026）遗产。巴基斯坦资深外交家艾哈迈德供职于联合国体系逾三十年，以副秘书长级别工作二十一年，是国际多边外交领域的重要人物之一。艾氏毕业于巴基斯坦旁遮普大学，后赴美国塔夫茨大学深造，专攻国际经济与国际法。1954年他以政治学讲师身份开启职业生涯，次年加入巴基斯坦外交部，1955至1969年间先后派驻开罗、渥太华及北京等地。1970年进入联合国秘书处，历任开发计划署高级顾问、经济及社会理事会秘书、秘书长办公厅主任、亚太经济社会委员会执行秘书等职。艾氏多次受命处理复杂国际事务，参与过东帝汶、柬埔寨、老挝—泰国冲突及缅甸等地区的调停。在1982年福克兰群岛危机和伊朗人质事件中发挥了重要作用。2003年又被任命为伊拉克问题特别顾问。他在2026年逝世，一生成就卓著，评价极高。本场委托的中国艺术品购自1960年代派驻北京巴基斯坦使馆任内。

This lot is located in Philadelphia.
Provenance:Property from the Private Collection of Dr. Augusta Rubin, acquired during her travels in Asia in 1963; thence by descent.Dr. Augusta Rubin was a highly accomplished classical pianist, musicologist, and professor at The Juilliard School, as well as the author of J.S. Bach: A Modern Composer. In 1963, she embarked on a pioneering solo voyage around the world, a remarkably independent undertaking for a woman of her era. Throughout her extensive travels across Asia, she cultivated a discerning eye and assembled a remarkable collection of art and antiquities. Preserved privately for over sixty years, this collection is now being presented to the public for the first time.來源：Augusta Rubin博士舊藏，1963年購於亞洲，后家族傳承。Augusta Rubin是一位造詣卓著的古典鋼琴家，並曾任教於茱莉亞音樂學院，著有巴赫傳記《J.S. Bach: A Modern Composer》。她曾與1963年環球單人旅行，這對當時的女性尤為難得，本場上拍的細密畫購于亞洲旅途。
